sections.hypothesis: On the day of a scheduled FOMC statement, holding the other six G10 currencies in our data against the US dollar (an equal-weight short-dollar basket) earns more than on other days, after spreads and a night's financing at retail CFD terms, 2006-02 to 2022-12.
sections.rationale: Who pays: Mueller, Tahbaz-Salehi and Vedolin (Journal of Finance 2017, 72(3), 1213-1252) find that a short-dollar portfolio of the ten most-traded currencies earns higher excess returns on scheduled FOMC announcement days (sample about 1994-2013), more for currencies whose rates are further above US rates, more when policy uncertainty is high, and more when the Fed eases. They read it as a premium paid to constrained intermediaries (dealers) for carrying monetary-policy uncertainty through the announcement: whoever needs dollar exposure hedged through the meeting pays them. A related paper on the same sample reports about 14.5 bps a day for the short-dollar strategy on FOMC days against 1.7 bps on other days (quoted in a search summary; not yet checked against the paper's tables). Against it: Borisenko and Pozdeev report the dollar's pre-announcement drift averaging to zero across specifications, and no clean post-2013 replication was found. Why it suits retail forex: finding 25 showed a strategy must earn more than its gross exposure times the broker's 1% financing markup every year; a position held about 8 days a year pays almost none of it, so only the spread matters. Not a variant of a rejected family: forex trend and carry (findings 25 and 26) held positions every day; this holds none outside announcement days. Independent of the crypto trend bets by construction.
sections.rules: The basket: long EUR, GBP, AUD and NZD against USD (EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD) and short USD against JPY, CHF and CAD (USDJPY, USDCHF, USDCAD), 1/7 of equity each, 1x gross, from our stored OANDA daily bid/ask bars (each bar 17:00 to 17:00 New York). An FOMC day is the bar containing a scheduled FOMC statement (the last day of each scheduled meeting, from the Federal Reserve's published calendars; unscheduled meetings and conference calls excluded), entered at its open and closed at its close: buying at the ask and selling at the bid, so the whole spread is paid, plus one night's financing per leg (rate difference less the 1% markup, from kestrel.data.rates, the month's known rate). Its net return is that day's basket return in AUD terms through the pairs' mids, as the forex engine accounts. 2006-02 to 2022-12 (about 136 meetings); the forex holdout (from 2023-01-01) is never read. Run once with kestrel fx-study fomc-dollar. A second run, also part of this study, uses daily bars ending 00:00 UTC (the statement still falls inside one bar), per the rule in TODO that a forex result must hold for both day ends.
sections.falsification: All needed, on the 17:00 New York bars, and tests 1 and 2 again on the 00:00 UTC bars: (1) the mean net return per FOMC day is above zero with its 95% interval (10,000 bootstrap resamples over meetings, seed 0) above zero; (2) it beats the same basket on random non-FOMC weekdays: above the 95th percentile of 1,000 sets of the same number of days, same costs; (3) after the paper's sample, 2014-01 to 2022-12, the mean net return is above zero (point estimate); (4) breadth: at least 5 of the 7 legs have a positive mean net return on FOMC days. PROCEED to a strategy note (fx-backtest, counted trials) only if all pass; otherwise KILL. Reported, deciding nothing: by year; easing meetings against the rest; high-yield legs (AUD, NZD) against low-yield (JPY, CHF); gross against net; the AUD/USD rate effect on the AUD account.
sections.parameters: None searched: the basket, the day definition and the costs are fixed above. 7 legs equal-weighted, 1x gross, one night's financing per meeting.
sections.costs: About 8 meetings a year, each a round trip on 7 pairs paying the full measured spread (median 1.4 bps EURUSD to 9.6 bps GBPJPY; this basket uses only USD pairs) and one night's financing with the 1% markup (about 0.3 bps a meeting at 1x). A study, not a trial: the forex pool stays at 2 (bar 0.11); a strategy note after a PROCEED would add its own trials.
